mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and corporate earnings are adversely affected.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 4% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment (UNRATE) show concurrent positive trends, it indicates a strong labor market, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS and UNRATE show positive trends but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter indicates reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines by more than 0.5% QoQ but the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals strong supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% MoM but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month indicates reduced demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines by more than 10% MoM but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and real GDP (GDPC1) is slowing, it indicates a tightening monetary policy that may negatively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4% and GDPC1 is slowing but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) in a tightening cycle increases borrowing costs, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in 3 months but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
